s2n-tls.version_output:
s2nc is an s2n-tls client testing utility.
It is not intended for production use.

usage: s2nc [options] host [port]
 host: hostname or IP address to connect to
 port: port to connect to

 Options:

  -a [protocols]
  --alpn [protocols]
    Sets the application protocols supported by this client, as a comma separated list.
  -c [version_string]
  --ciphers [version_string]
    Set the cipher preference version string. Defaults to "default" 
  --enter-fips-mode
    Enter libcrypto's FIPS mode. The linked version of OpenSSL must be built with the FIPS module.
  -e,--echo
    Listen to stdin after TLS Connection is established and echo it to the Server
  --send-file [file path]
    Sends the contents of the provided file to the server after connecting.
  -h,--help
    Display this message and quit.
  -n [server name]
  --name [server name]
    Sets the SNI server name header for this client.  If not specified, the host value is used.
  -s,--status
    Request the OCSP status of the remote server certificate
  -m,--mfl
    Request maximum fragment length from: 512, 1024, 2048, 4096
  -f,--ca-file [file path]
    Location of trust store CA file (PEM format). If neither -f or -d are specified. System defaults will be used.
  -d,--ca-dir [directory path]
    Directory containing hashed trusted certs. If neither -f or -d are specified. System defaults will be used.
  -i,--insecure
    Turns off certification validation altogether.
  -l,--cert [file path]
    Path to a PEM encoded certificate. Optional. Will only be used for client auth
  -k,--key [file path]
    Path to a PEM encoded private key that matches cert. Will only be used for client auth
  -r,--reconnect
    Drop and re-make the connection using Session ticket. If session ticket is disabled, then re-make the connection using Session-ID 
  -T,--no-session-ticket 
    Disable session ticket for resumption.
  --ticket-out [file path]
    Path to a file where the session ticket can be stored.
  --ticket-in [file path]
    Path to session ticket file to resume connection.
  -D,--dynamic
    Set dynamic record resize threshold
  -t,--timeout
    Set dynamic record timeout threshold
  -C,--corked-io
    Turn on corked io
  -B,--non-blocking
    Set the non-blocking flag on the connection's socket.
  -L --key-log <path>
    Enable NSS key logging into the provided path
  -P --psk <psk-identity,psk-secret,psk-hmac-alg> 
    A comma-separated list of psk parameters in this order: psk_identity, psk_secret and psk_hmac_alg.
    Note that the maximum number of permitted psks is 10, the psk-secret is hex-encoded, and whitespace is not allowed before or after the commas.
    Ex: --psk psk_id,psk_secret,SHA256 --psk shared_id,shared_secret,SHA384.
  -E ,--early-data <file path>
    Sends data in file path as early data to the server. Early data will only be sent if s2nc receives a session ticket and resumes a session.
  --renegotiation [accept|reject]
    accept: Accept all server requests for a new handshake
    reject: Reject all server requests for a new handshake
  --npn 
    Indicates support for the NPN extension. The '--alpn' option MUST be used with this option to signal the protocols supported.
  --buffered-send <buffer size>
    Set s2n_send to buffer up to <buffer size> bytes before sending records over the wire.
  --prefer-low-latency
    Prefer low latency by clamping maximum outgoing record size at 1500.
  --prefer-throughput
    Prefer throughput by raising maximum outgoing record size to 16k
